According to the latest report from Bloomberg, the head of Apple Pay and Wallet will retire in October. Jennifer Bailey joined Apple in the early 2000s and has served as vice president of Apple Pay since 2014.

Apple Pay主管將於十月退休

The news was announced by Eddy Cue, senior vice president of Services, through an internal memo, in which he praised Bailey's contributions to the company. Cue stated that Apple will announce succession arrangements before Bailey's departure in October:

"After more than 25 years at Apple, Jennifer Bailey has decided to retire in October. During her tenure, Jennifer made outstanding contributions, from leading the Apple Store online store through a period of significant growth and global expansion, to overseeing the launch of Apple Pay. We will announce a succession plan before Jennifer completes the handover at the end of October, and Jennifer will continue to support the transition in an advisory capacity."

According to Bloomberg, Bailey's departure is regarded as a "major loss" within Apple.

Bailey joined Apple in the early 2000s and began leading the Apple online store team from 2003. She was subsequently promoted to vice president of Apple Pay in 2014, the same year the payment platform officially launched. She was also responsible for overseeing Apple Wallet. Over the years, Bailey has been a familiar face at Apple launch events.

Today's report from Bloomberg also revealed that Josh Rosenstock will be leaving Apple in what was described as an "unrelated move." Rosenstock is Apple's senior director of corporate communications, responsible for the company's financial and investor public relations work.

These personnel changes come as Apple prepares for John Ternus to succeed Tim Cook as CEO on September 1.
